clue.text: Desire to include navy and leaders of private institutes in dance

indicators.note: the word for desire is opened up to take in the other letters

parts.note: to desire something is to hope for it
RN is the Royal Navy

indicators.note: the leaders of the two words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: Someone longs to bring sailors and the heads of private colleges into a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include' signals insertion and 'leaders of' takes the opening letters; 'Desire' reads as a verb but supplies the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: A hornpipe is a lively solo dance traditionally associated with sailors.

clue.text: Interruption has annoyed lecturer, tetchy, just starting

indicators.note: only the starting letter of each of these four words is used

explanation.surface: A grumpy lecturer is irritated at being interrupted.
explanation.definitionFit: A halt is a stop or pause, an interruption in progress.

clue.text: Small drink for each child

parts.note: a nip is a small measure of spirits
per means for each, as in 'per head'

explanation.surface: Ordering a small drink for every child in the group.
explanation.definitionFit: Nipper is an informal British word for a small child.

clue.text: Old ruler needing some vodka is erratic

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An old monarch needs a little vodka and behaves unpredictably.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'needing', but that is the link word joining definition to wordplay; 'Old ruler' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Kaiser was the title of the German and Austrian emperors, rulers now consigned to history.

clue.text: Douglas native perhaps one's left with monarch

parts.note: one is I, and one's is short for one is, giving I plus S
and means together with
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A Douglas native, perhaps, is left alone with the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Douglas is the capital of the Isle of Man, so someone born there is an islander; 'perhaps' marks this as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone born in Douglas, capital of the Isle of Man, is an example of an island inhabitant.

clue.text: Rush from fine shelter

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: Hurrying out of a pleasant shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee is to run away from a place or danger, rushing from it.

clue.text: Maladroit, alas, I'm no famous smiler?

indicators.note: maladroit means clumsy, so these letters are handled clumsily and come out rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone clumsy laments that they are no famous smiler.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo's portrait is world-renowned for the sitter's enigmatic smile.

clue.text: Prices down in this Northern town?

definitions.meaning: a period when shops cut their prices
A town near Manchester in the north of England

explanation.surface: Wondering whether this northern town is where prices have dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop event with reduced prices; also the name of a town in Greater Manchester.

clue.text: Fashionable tame animals round part of foot

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'

indicators.note: turned round, so the word for tame animals is read backwards

parts.note: pets are tame animals kept at home

explanation.surface: Trendy pets walking around someone's feet.
explanation.definitionFit: The instep is the arched middle section of the foot between toes and ankle.

clue.text: Small walk leading to unoccupied area

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
to pace is to walk with measured steps

explanation.surface: A short stroll ends up at an empty patch of ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A space is an empty region or gap with nothing in it.

clue.text: Regularly retype for organ

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Retyping a document over and over for an organ, perhaps a newsletter.
explanation.definitionFit: The eye is the body's organ of sight.

clue.text: Bird not finishing beer

indicators.note: the bird's name stops short, losing its final letter

parts.note: the bittern is a wading bird of the heron family

explanation.surface: A bird leaves its pint of beer unfinished.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter is a traditional English draught ale, well hopped.

clue.text: Unyielding about incomplete bequest list in period of decline

indicators.note: the word for unyielding goes about, around, the shortened document

parts.note: tight can mean rigid or unyielding

indicators.note: the document's name loses its last letter

parts.note: a will is the document listing someone's bequests

explanation.surface: Someone stubborn over a partial list of bequests in their declining years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' drops the last letter of the document, and 'about' wraps the word for unyielding around what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilight figuratively means the final stage of decline, as in 'the twilight of his career'.

clue.text: More insulting about daughter? This should give guidance

indicators.note: the word for more insulting goes around the single letter

parts.note: ruder means more insulting or offensive
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Being nastier about one's daughter, wondering if this counts as guidance.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat's rudder is the device that steers it, guiding its course.

clue.text: Blokes kept in by nasty sleet weather?

indicators.note: the word for blokes is held inside the other letters
nasty suggests the word sleet is messed up and its letters rearranged

parts.note: blokes are men

explanation.surface: Men stay indoors because of horrible sleet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' rearranges the sleet, and 'kept in by' holds the blokes inside that rearrangement; the question mark flags weather as a loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out in the elements means being exposed to wind, rain and the weather in general.

clue.text: Many for example embraced by celebrity

indicators.note: the abbreviation is held inside the word for a celebrity

parts.note: a lion is a celebrated person, as in 'literary lion'
eg is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Plenty of people, for instance, are hugged by a famous person.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, legion means very numerous: 'their fans are legion'.

clue.text: Northern worker at heart of best European port

parts.note: an ant is the classic crossword worker, from the worker ant

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letters

explanation.surface: A northern labourer at the centre of Europe's finest harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart of' takes ES from the middle of 'best'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nantes is a city and port on the Loire in western France.

clue.text: Set of programmes has notices about Rhode Island

indicators.note: the word for notices goes around the state abbreviation

parts.note: to notice something is to see it
RI is the US postal abbreviation for Rhode Island

explanation.surface: A TV run of shows features adverts about Rhode Island.
explanation.definitionFit: A series is a sequence of related television or radio programmes.

clue.text: About to get involved in religious group — not many know it

indicators.note: involved in means placed within the word for the religious group

parts.note: a sect is a religious group
re means about or concerning, as in letters

explanation.surface: Joining a religious group about which few people know anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Something known to only a few people is by definition confidential.

clue.text: Do the same as primate

definitions.meaning: a large tailless primate such as a chimpanzee

explanation.surface: Copying a monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: To imitate is to mimic, and a gorilla or chimpanzee is a primate.

clue.text: Youngster born with attitude getting name

parts.note: an air is a manner or attitude, as in 'an air of confidence'

explanation.surface: A young person, born with attitude, getting named.
explanation.definitionFit: Bairn is the Scottish and northern English word for a child.

clue.text: The two clubs put off by poor quality repair

indicators.note: the clubs letter is put off, removed, from the word for a bad repair

parts.note: a botch is a clumsy, badly done repair
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Two golf clubs rejected because of a shoddy repair.
explanation.definitionFit: Both refers to two things together, the pair of them.

clue.text: Colluders allowed to return following vehicle

indicators.note: the turned word comes after the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: the word for allowed comes back, read the other way

parts.note: to let means to allow

explanation.surface: Conspirators let back in to follow a getaway car.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartel is a group of firms colluding to fix prices or limit competition.

clue.text: Managed to overlook a thousand — highly offensive!

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits above, overlooking, the other

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it, past tense ran
K is the abbreviation for a thousand, from kilo

explanation.surface: Someone in charge ignored a thousand, which is deeply offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlook' hints at ignoring something, but in this down entry it means sitting above.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank as an adjective means foul-smelling or grossly offensive.

clue.text: Channel shunned by Duke showing restless desire

indicators.note: the duke's letter is shunned, left out of the channel

parts.note: a ditch is a narrow channel for water

explanation.surface: A duke avoiding a TV channel shows he is restless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' suggests television, but here it is a ditch dug for water.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a restless craving, as in 'an itch to travel'.

clue.text: Description of ring man heading off brought to Northern Ireland — extremely tacky

indicators.note: the man's name loses its first letter

parts.note: Peter is a man's name

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Describing a ring a man brought to Belfast that turned out very tacky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' leaves ETER from PETER; 'extremely' gives TY from 'tacky'.
explanation.definitionFit: An eternity ring is a band set with stones all round, symbolising never-ending love.
